body.x: PiVIS Tech Company (CEO Yeongseob Kueon) will attend CES 2025 from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas. It will showcase its groundbreaking e-nose solution, Deep U-Nose AI, at the K-Startup Pavilion.

PiVIS is a leader in developing AI-powered “electronic nose” solutions capable of detecting sub-ppb (parts per billion) levels of odors and smells. Known for its exceptional capabilities in AI applications using machine learning and deep learning, PiVIS has built a solid reputation for providing tailored solutions for manufacturing industries. These solutions ensure the evaluation and verification of systems, facilities, and products, earning the company substantial trust despite its relatively short operational history.
At CES 2025, PiVIS will expand its focus from manufacturing to healthcare with Deep U-Nose AI, a solution designed to analyze urine odors to enable early detection of diseases, including cancer.

Deep U-Nose AI’s sensing system integrates into toilet seats and lids as a noninvasive sampling device, ensuring seamless health monitoring without disrupting users’ daily routines. The collector is equipped with odor sensor arrays that detect trace biomarkers in urine. The collected data is analyzed through a deep learning ensemble model to identify early signs of diseases or cancers. Results are transmitted to connected devices, such as smartphones, allowing users to monitor their health in real-time and take necessary actions.

A PiVIS representative explained, “Deep U-Nose AI addresses the growing demand for early diagnosis in aging societies and aims to improve cancer survival rates. It enables users to monitor their health effortlessly at home while leveraging AI precision and continuous learning to enhance accuracy over time.”

The company noted that Deep U-Nose AI has achieved a 95% disease detection accuracy and plans to commercialize the product next year. By debuting it at CES 2025, PiVIS aims to showcase its technological excellence on a global stage.

PiVIS also plans to extend its e-nose technology to respiratory and diagnostic medical systems, with expansion efforts targeting North America, the European Union (EU), Japan, and Singapore. “Through Deep U-Nose AI, we intend to redefine how people manage their health and bring innovative diagnostic solutions to the global market,” the representative added.
